items.title: Look Past UI with Deep Design
items.summary: Rent the Runway, Uber, and Airbnb challenge the traditional experiences of their industries through deep design, not just screen-UI design.

items.title: Narrative Biases: When Storytelling HURTS User Experience
items.summary: Overreliance on narrative details and assumptions about cause-and-effect explanations can lead to errors in judgment by UX practitioners.

items.title: UX Research Cheat Sheet
items.summary: User research can be done at any point in the design cycle. This list of methods and activities can help you decide which to use when.

items.title: The Sketch Test: How to Test and Improve Your UX Deliverables and Other Documents
items.summary: Test your infographics, reports, and UX deliverables with representative colleagues to refine them and prevent potential stakeholder misunderstandings.

items.title: Ideation for Everyday Design Challenges
items.summary: Improve your UI design solutions by considering many ideas before settling on any one of them. A solid ideation methodology broadens your idea-generation capacity.

items.title: UX Stories Communicate Designs
items.summary: Help internal audiences empathize with users and buy into your design goals with well-crafted stories that build insight and focus on users and their needs.

items.title: What Are Personas and Why Should I Care?
items.summary: Personas can humanize complex data and help give UX design teams a consistent focus and design target.

items.title: Design Critiques: Encourage a Positive Culture to Improve Products
items.summary: Open feedback is essential for a collaborative UX process.

items.title: Journey Mapping in Real Life: A Survey of UX Practitioners
items.summary: Successful journey maps need to be focused on a clear business goal, well communicated in the organization, and truthful to user needs.

items.title: Design Thinking Builds Strong Teams
items.summary: Not only does design thinking foster innovation, but it also strengthens teams by creating common vocabulary and artifacts, and a trust-based team culture.

items.title: Top 10 Tips for UX Success From Agile Practitioners
items.summary: 125 practitioners share their experience and success stories for improving user experience in Agile projects.

items.title: Minimize Design Risk by Focusing on Outcomes Not Features
items.summary: Resist the urge to lead with implementation. Once you know what the need is, you’ll know what to build.

items.title: Design Thinking 101
items.summary: Design thinking is a user-centered process that helps teams understand needs, generate ideas, test solutions, and drive innovation.

items.title: When and How to Create Customer Journey Maps
items.summary: Journey maps combine two powerful instruments—storytelling and visualization—in order to help teams understand and address customer needs.

items.title: Front-End Style-Guides: Definition, Requirements, Component Checklist
items.summary: Front-end style guides help efficient design and testing, and enforce UI consistency. We present 8 style-guide requirements and 25 common components.

items.title: How UX Professionals Collaborate on Deliverables
items.summary: 82% of UX professionals collaborate with other team members to produce deliverables. Ideation workshops and “four-eyes” reviews occur frequently, both in-person and remotely. In addition, the roles and contributions of collaborators vary widely.

items.title: Which UX Deliverables Are Most Commonly Created and Shared?
items.summary: Static wireframes are the most popular UX deliverable, but 11 different deliverable formats were used by at least half the professionals we surveyed.

items.title: Test Paper Prototypes to Save Time and Money: The Mozilla Case Study
items.summary: Low-fidelity user testing of several iterations of Mozilla’s Support website quickly showed which user-interface elements worked best for Firefox users.

items.title: UX Without User Research Is Not UX
items.summary: UX teams are responsible for creating desirable experiences for users. Yet many organizations fail to include users in the development process. Without customer input, organizations risk creating interfaces that fail.

items.title: Charrettes (Design Sketching): ½ Inspiration, ½ Buy-In
items.summary: Design charrettes inspire design sketches and ideas, include more people in the design process, explore and expose goals and objectives of colleagues in multiple functional roles, and drive off designer’s block.
